t353_regression_finding: 🔴 THIS IS THE REASON THIS BATCH IS SMALL AND FULL-APPARATUS, NOT WORD-ONLY. T-353 (plan/50-tasks.md: ✅ C-0800) DID land word-only-row support in lib/core/contentSchema.ts/batchRecord.ts/build-ingest-sql.mjs — verified live by reading the code (gateSense accepts examples:null with items:[]/distractors:[] together). A first draft of this tick wrote 269 word-only Tier-1 rows (the full remaining Tier-1 gap) and ran clean through npm run measure:gate (0 rejected) and the four build:* generators. BUT npm run verify — the actual gate before push — failed on two tests that were NOT updated when T-353 landed: scripts/measure-gate.test.ts ('gates two example sentences per row — D-022, counted and not assumed', asserting `sentencesGated === SOURCE_ROWS * 2`) and scripts/build-ingest-sql.test.ts ('emits exactly two examples per PASSING sense — D-022'). Isolated with `git stash` + `npx vitest run scripts/measure-gate.test.ts`: 4/4 green without any word-only row in the bank, 1/4 red with even ONE word-only row present — confirmed via a throwaway single-row test, not inferred. This means word-only mode is currently unusable by CONTENT: the code path exists but the verify suite actively rejects it. The 269-row word-only batch was discarded (git restore/rm, never committed) and this 16-word full-apparatus batch was written instead so the tick still ends with green, shippable work. Reported to plan/03-for-roy.md and plan/80-content-lessons.md lesson 62 (CONTENT cannot edit plan/60-findings.md or code itself). Recommend DEV update both tests to sum each row's actual example count instead of assuming a flat 2-per-row multiplier, so word-only rows (Roy's 14/09 volume instruction) become usable.
gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) run via `npm run measure:gate` against all 49 batch files (1,691 rows after this tick — down from 1,944 because the discarded 269-row draft was never committed; 3,382 example sentences · 5,073 item stems re-gated): 0 rejected. First draft had 2 stems over the 14-word ceiling (steak L3, wine L3, target L3, one more caught in the same pass) — shortened and re-gated, 0/0 rejected on the second pass. Every background word in every example and stem was checked with `grep -x` against data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt BEFORE writing (§A1 rule 1) — 9 headwords needed a substitution (steak: chef/herbs -> cook/rice; spoon: soup -> food; suitcase: airport -> station; treasure: pirates/hid/jewels/hidden/divers/sunken -> gold/silver/kept/coast/lost; wine: grapes -> fruit; wedding: bride/groom/thousands -> couple/danced/many; university: thousands -> many; sunglasses: sunlight/cloudy -> sun/laughed; target: arrow -> stone/ball/wall), verified 0 remaining vocabulary issues before the gate ran.
distractor_review_note: Every distractor was checked by hand for the near-synonym trap (lesson-file §A1 rule 2 / lesson 24): first draft had statue/sculpture (near-identical), stadium/arena (near-identical), target/goal+aim (near-identical to the abstract sense used in the neutral example) — all three replaced (statue -> painting/photograph; stadium -> museum/hospital; target's neutral example rewritten to the concrete sense only, distractors -> wall/board) before finalizing. gateSense does not check distractor words against allowed-words (same open, unresolved gap recorded in prior manifests since 12-13/09) — distractors here are simple, common English nouns at or below A2 by inspection, not machine-verified.
he_one_to_many_note: Every translation_he grepped against every existing translation_he in data/generated/batch-*.jsonl. Two benign collisions, both legitimate near-synonyms sharing one Hebrew word, not errors: 'stomach'->בטן / 'belly'->בטן; 'target'->מטרה / 'purpose'->מטרה. Not tagged he_one_to_many_group (that field is for one Hebrew word spanning several senses of THIS batch's own headwords, not cross-batch synonym overlap) and not rewritten.
translation_confidence_note: 16/16 rows are translation_confidence:"high" — every headword in this batch is a concrete, unambiguous A2 noun with one clear Hebrew translation for the sense written.
